newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium vows to keep health spending down for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Belgium vows to keep health spending down for EMU.

text.p: The Belgian government will monitor health spending monthly to keep new borrowing within targets agreed for a single European currency, Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Monday.

"There has been a decision to put the health sector under permanent monitoring. Notably, the government will make an evaluation of the situation in the sector every month and will take the necessary measures to meet the (budgetary) norms of the government agreement," Maystadt told a news conference.
He was speaking after a meeting of European Union finance ministers.

Belgium is striving to keep its deficit below the three percent of gross domestic product targetted for European economic and monetary union (EMU). Last year's deficit was 3.4 percent. The ratio is forecast to fall to 2.9 percent or under in 1997.
Maystadt said that his EU colleagues, who said earlier they consider Belgium's convergence plan for EMU credible and adequate, had expressed worries about recent overshooting in health spending.
At the end of last year, Belgium took an extra 20 billion Belgian francs of austerity measures in the health section of the social security budget in order to keep its deficit target on track.
